claims.claim: .NET is slower to cold-start than Node or Go
claims.about: C# / ASP.NET Core vs Node (Express, Fastify) and Go (Gin, net/http)
claims.measured: Start-up: csharp-aspnet 785 ms; node-express 706 ms, node-fastify 593 ms; go-gin 293 ms, go-nethttp 238 ms
claims.why: The measured container start-up times point the same way: .NET is slowest of the three, slightly slower than Node and about 2.7–3.3x slower than Go, though Azure Functions host cold start itself is not measured.

claims.claim: Node (TypeScript): cold starts are usually lower [than .NET]
claims.measured: Start-up: node-express 706 ms, node-fastify 593 ms vs csharp-aspnet 785 ms
claims.why: Both Node servers started faster than ASP.NET Core, by about 10–25%.

claims.measured: Start-up: go-nethttp 238 ms, go-gin 293 ms vs node 593–706 ms, csharp-aspnet 785 ms
claims.why: Go had the lowest start-up of the three options considered, tied with Rust for the lowest in the whole benchmark.

claims.claim: Most of the cold-start time is in the team's own startup code (DI container, Cosmos/Service Bus clients, Key Vault secrets), not in the runtime
claims.why: The benchmark measures only bare server start-up; it doesn't measure app initialisation code or how Azure Functions cold starts break down.

claims.claim: ReadyToRun compilation, trimming dependencies and lazy client initialisation reduce startup cost
claims.why: The measurements don't compare .NET builds with and without ReadyToRun or other startup optimisations.
